longForm.heroLead: Erratic powder discharge is expensive. Arching, rat-holing, unplanned downtime. Problems that usually get discovered on the production line, when it's too late to fix cheaply. PFT Powder Flow Tester catches them before they happen, on the bench. A complete full flow function test runs in just 25 minutes, fast enough to actually inform formulation decisions instead of trailing them. Nine distinct measurements come out of that testing: bulk density, wall friction, flow index, arching dimensions, rat-hole diameter, hopper half angle, Carr Index, Hausner Ratio, and time consolidation. The solution is compact enough for any workbench. No dedicated lab space required. Powder Flow Pro software runs the whole workflow, and results export directly to Excel for downstream analysis and reporting. What it prevents: costly downtime from erratic powder discharge. What it produces: the data needed to write consistent Standard Operating Procedures. Where it fits: formulation, characterization, and QA/QC, one solution across all three.

sections.title: The Nine Measurements
sections.description: What each output tells you about handling behavior.
body: A single flow function number doesn't tell a hopper designer everything they need. PFT's testing produces nine distinct outputs, each answering a different practical question about how a powder will actually behave in equipment.

Bulk density, measured at fill and final states, establishes the baseline the rest of the data builds from. Wall friction predicts how the powder interacts with the specific material a hopper or chute is built from, not a generic assumption. Flow index summarizes overall flowability. Arching dimensions and rat-hole diameter predict the two most common hopper discharge failures before either happens on the production line. Hopper half angle informs the actual geometry a new hopper needs. Carr Index and Hausner Ratio flag compressibility and caking risk. Time consolidation testing, run alongside the full flow function data, captures how flow behavior changes after a powder has sat in storage, a condition standard single-point testing misses entirely.
